newsitem.title: UK: Euro refiner seeks gas oil price link to Brent.
newsitem.headline: Euro refiner seeks gas oil price link to Brent.

text.p: A European refiner has proposed linking the price of Mediterranean gas oil sales to the spot value of Brent crude to shore up sagging profit margins, traders said on Thursday.
The proposal by Italy's Isab SpA would ignore the current formula used by the industry which values gas oil as a differential to Platt's Med cif and fob quotations.
The proposal, canvassed in informal conversations with Mediterranean distillate traders, has met a mixed reaction tinged heavily with scepticism.
"If they want to pass the risk of refining to the traders as well as the risk of trading margins, they can forget it," said one British-based critic.

The proposal would involve buyers and sellers agreeing a profit margin, expressing the margin in terms of a simple ratio, multiplying the ratio by the spot value of international benchmark Dated Brent and converting the result into dollars per tonne.

The plan, a kind of reverse netback arrangement, appears to face a daunting challenge from end-users who prefer to stick to traditional gas oil-related contracts and who might well end up paying more under a formula linked to Brent.
While the other main buyers -- trading houses -- can always hedge against paper, many would resent being forced to take on extra risk, analysts say.
"It's very difficult to change the psychology of the market," said another trader at a large European oil company. "We cannot buy for our affiliates on this basis because they are used to Platt's."
Refining margins in the Mediterranean improved by around 30 cents a barrel this week to around $1.88 for a complex cracker and $0.45 for a simple refinery.
But the margins remain 50 cents to $1 a barrel below the best 1997 levels seen so far in June and May.
The meagre earnings have led ISAB's Melilli refinery in Sicily to cut gas oil output to around 350,000 tonnes a month from around 450,000 tonnes, traders said.
The spread between heating oil and more expensive EN590 low sulphur diesel has narrowed in the Mediterranean to around $5 a tonne on Platt's.
This is around $5 or $6 below the spread refiners say they need to make EN590 output worthwhile.
Some refiners said the ISAB proposal was worth study but in order to be accepted the formula would have to be seen to offer customers more benefits.
"In times of poor margins it might make sense to try to build in a guaranteed 20 percent margin by using a 1.20 multiple in the formula," one trader said.
"But when margins are good they'll be shooting themselves in the foot because they could get 25 percent margin by normal pricing," he said.
And the proposal merely begged the question as to why ISAB did not use paper to hedge their risk in the futures and swaps markets.
"I appreciate why they are trying to do. We should study it. We have been talking about the pricing issue in general, among ourselves," one Italian refiner said.
